requirements.requirement: node1 configured to run a DHCP server on the private network shared with node2 and node3
requirements.summary: node1 (VyOS) eth1 was configured with static address 10.50.50.254/24 and a Kea DHCP server (shared-network LAN, subnet 10.50.50.0/24, range .100-.200, default-router/name-server options, 3600s lease) was committed and saved to config.boot. The running kea-dhcp4.conf and process (ps aux) confirm the service is live, and after-executor listening-sockets show kea-dhcp4 bound to 10.50.50.254:67. Both intended DHCP clients successfully received leases from this server, directly confirming the server is functioning on the shared network.

requirements.requirement: node2 configured to obtain its private-network address from node1 via DHCP instead of static assignment
requirements.summary: /etc/network/interfaces on node2 was changed to 'iface eth1 inet dhcp'; networking restart logs show dhcpcd soliciting and receiving a lease (10.50.50.100) explicitly 'from 10.50.50.254' (node1). Subsequent ip addr/route output confirms the dynamic-scope address and a default route via node1. node1's lease database independently recorded this lease under hostname 'node2'.

requirements.requirement: node3 configured to obtain its private-network address from node1 via DHCP instead of static assignment
requirements.summary: Same change applied to node3: /etc/network/interfaces set eth1 to dhcp; dhcpcd log shows lease 10.50.50.101 offered/leased 'from 10.50.50.254'; ip addr/route confirms dynamic address and default route via node1; node1's lease CSV independently recorded the lease under hostname 'node3'.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all managed nodes with pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/config state
requirements.summary: All three nodes show a complete bounded-disruption transition: pre-restart boot_id capture, an explicit reboot command, a period of connection failures consistent with the node being down, then a new boot_id, followed by direct recovery checks. node1's changed boot_id (36437d9e) and recovered eth1 address, running kea-dhcp4 process, intact lease file and persisted config.boot match the fixed after-executor snapshot. node2 and node3 changed boot_ids (20a60135, 310f1fc4) match their after-executor snapshots, and both automatically re-acquired their prior DHCP-assigned addresses (10.50.50.100/.101) from node1 on boot, confirming the DHCP-client configuration is itself persistent. A final check after all three reboots shows node1's kea-dhcp4 still running with fresh renewed leases from both clients, confirming end-to-end service continuity.

overall_summary: All material contract requirements are satisfied with direct evidence: node1 runs a committed, persisted Kea DHCP server on the shared 10.50.50.0/24 network, and node2/node3 were reconfigured from static to DHCP on eth1, both successfully leasing addresses from node1 (confirmed independently via client-side logs/ip output and server-side lease-database records). The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also executed cleanly on all three nodes, with baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and full recovery of network, DHCP-server, and lease state directly observed and cross-checked against the fixed after-executor snapshots.
limitations: One node1 configuration attempt (cmd-44ea90c00f914f7c) used invalid CLI syntax and failed at commit; the mechanism by which the eth1 static address later appeared applied (despite this failed, allegedly-unsaved commit) is not fully explained by the captured trace, though the final committed config.boot and running state are self-consistent and correct.

Kea's interfaces-config uses the VyOS-generated default 'interfaces: ["*"]', so the DHCP server technically listens on all interfaces (including the mgmt network) rather than being scoped to eth1 only; this is standard VyOS template behavior rather than an executor misconfiguration, and no evidence shows it caused any unintended lease assignment on the mgmt network.

operational_hygiene.summary: The command trace is largely composed of read-only discovery (find/grep/cat of VyOS templates and config, ip/link inspection) needed to locate the current Kea-based dhcp-server CLI syntax after legacy isc-dhcp-style syntax failed, plus the minimal state changes required to satisfy the task: bringing up eth1 on node2/node3 (cmd-958abbad28294280, cmd-ff5323f2ce48459d), rewriting /etc/network/interfaces on both Alpine nodes (cmd-8f6829db18a647e7, cmd-994013818f1e44c2), and configuring/committing the DHCP server on node1. One state-changing command, cmd-44ea90c00f914f7c, attempted an invalid dhcp-server configuration (subnet-parameters/default-router/name-server at the wrong level) which failed at commit ('Commit failed... uncommitted changes that will not be saved'); since VyOS discards uncommitted edits on session exit and the following successful commit (cmd-8100ac44f3484119) used corrected syntax, this failed attempt left no residue but is counted as a bounded, self-corrected troubleshooting mutation. The three sequential single-node reboots were necessary to satisfy the independent restart-evidence protocol. Post-task snapshots show no failed services, no unexpected package-health issues (only a pre-existing chrony.drift diff on Alpine nodes carried over unchanged from before-prepare), and only expected residue (per-boot systemd-private tmp dirs, /tmp/reboot.log from the reboot helper script) with no unexplained leftover files or exposed services beyond the intended DHCP server.
